subject: Window seats with integrated storage
hook: Bay windows are rarely square. That's where the design work starts.
ig:
Bay windows are rarely square. That's where the design work starts.

Here's how a typical window seat goes from awkward bay to everyday seat:

1. Survey. We measure every angle and width, plus the sill, sockets and radiator.
2. Use. A reading nook wants more depth; a dining bench wants table height in mind.
3. Storage. Drawers for things you reach for daily, lift-up for bulky things, a vented front if the radiator stays.
4. Finish. Matched to the room or the alcove units either side.
5. Workshop. Cut, edged, drilled and assembled in Hanley.
6. Fit. Scribed to the bay so there's no gap at the walls.

The odd angles are why off-the-shelf benches rarely fit a bay, and why made-to-measure does.

Tap the link in bio to see finished SUPERIO projects.
fb:
Ever tried fitting an off-the-shelf bench into a bay window? The angles never quite work.

That's why a made-to-measure window seat starts with a careful survey, then a few decisions: how you'll use it, what storage suits, and which finish ties it into the room. It's made in our Hanley workshop and scribed to the walls on site.

You can see finished SUPERIO work on our showcase page.

on_asset:
F1: Survey the bay — Angles, widths at several heights, sill height, sockets and anything below the window. |
F2: Decide how it's used — Reading nook, dining bench or toy storage changes the depth, height and storage type. |
F3: Choose the storage — Soft-close drawers for daily items, lift-up for bulky ones, vented front if there's a radiator. |
F4: Match the room — Finish and handles chosen to sit with surrounding furniture or the alcove units either side. |
F5: Made in the workshop — Panels cut, edged, drilled and assembled in Hanley, then checked before they leave. |
F6: Fit and scribe — Installed and scribed to the bay so the seat sits tight to every wall. |
